features.headline: Breaking down the CFP race for three conferences after Week 10
features.desc: The margin between winning the conference and making the CFP is considerably wider for certain teams.
body: We're entering Week 11 of the college football season, and yet, somehow less time means more questions. Nobody seems to know what to do with the Heisman, and I'm not seeing a price worth chasing right now.
For the record, Notre Dame QB CJ Carr (+220), Miami QB Darian Mensah (+250) and Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith (+280) are the three favorites.
The national title board hasn't moved enough to change my mind, either. So, let's look elsewhere.
Who will make the playoff? Who will win their conference? Between the remaining schedules and tiebreakers, there's plenty to sort through before we put money on any of it.

I went into the MAC thinking 7-2 Ohio might be the play. The Bobcats are undefeated in conference play, host Toledo (7-2 overall, 4-1 MAC) in Week 13 and boom: +295 to win it. There's something there.
But then I looked at how those teams match up, and Toledo's defense kept getting in the way. Ohio wants to run. Toledo is really good at stopping it, and it also has a much better passing game.
So now I'm looking at Ohio's bigger payout and asking whether I actually like the matchup or just the number.

Toledo at +146 isn't exactly giving us some huge discount. Western Michigan (6-3, 4-1 MAC) has a manageable schedule left, but I don't trust its offense as much. I can make a case for all three getting to the championship game. I'm less interested in paying these prices to find out which one does.

Memphis (7-2, 4-1 AAC) was the team I kept looking at in the American. I like Marcus Stokes and the passing game. I trust the Tigers' pass defense more than North Texas' or UTSA's. But Memphis still has to go to South Florida and Navy.

features.headline: Commanders running low on time to 'put it all together'
features.desc: Dan Quinn knows it's repetitive to say the Commanders are close, but now they're painted into a corner.
body: LANDOVER, Md. — Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels didn't hesitate. After yet another loss, and after falling three games under.500, Daniels — and his teammates — know that their season is slipping away.
So, when asked Sunday night if he worried they had enough time to turn it around, he quickly replied, "Yeah. Next week is a must win."
Earlier teammate K'Lavon Chaisson said, "Yeah, damn right" when asked a similar question.
Unfortunately for the Commanders it's a familiar place. But it's also indicative of their season. At 2-5-1, they're three games behind the New York Giants (5-2-1) in the NFC East.

Mathematically the Commanders remain alive, but with nine games remaining, any realistic hope the team has for a strong finish likely begins and ends vs. the Giants on Thursday. A win and they would be two games back with eight to play and own the tiebreaker — if that eventually mattered.
"We all know how badly we need this," Washington coach Dan Quinn said. "Everyone in this building understands that."

Another loss would drop them to 7-18-1 since the start of last season and likely intensify the speculation by analysts over Quinn's future. Owner Josh Harris has not publicly commented on Quinn's job. Quinn said he regularly meets with Harris before and after games and also on Mondays.
But in training camp one team source said what has been repeated by others at various points, "It's a results business."

And the results need to improve. Washington has now played five one-score games; the Commanders are 1-3-1 in those games — and 3-7-1 since the start of 2025. In 2024, when they went 12-5, Washington was 8-4 in one-score games — but that included a four-game winning streak at season's end.

features.headline: Cooper Flagg breaks down in-game peanut butter and jelly sandwich
features.desc: Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg has recently started eating an in-game peanut butter and jelly sandwich.
body: With a comfortable lead against the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday, Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg headed to the bench for good early in the fourth quarter. He put on his warmups, sat next to teammate Daniel Gafford and watched the Mavericks close out a 130-93 victory.
Moments later, the Mavericks' TV broadcast caught Flagg with a small plastic bag in hand, taking out a peanut butter and jelly sandwich and having a bite.
"Boy, that looks good right now," former Mavericks guard Derek Harper said on the broadcast.
It marked the second consecutive game Flagg enjoyed a peanut butter and jelly sandwich during the action.

Last Friday, his in-game meal came during a 112-100 win over the Utah Jazz in which he racked up 21 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists and three steals. Cameras similarly spotted him taking a bite. Flagg followed that up with 25 points, a career-high 12 assists and five rebounds in Sunday's game.

Not surprisingly, reporters asked the second-year forward about his in-game snack. He first nodded to the Mavs' strength and medical staff before clarifying that he's trying to put on weight and gain muscle.

"So those requirements I got to meet. I'm just trying to stay ahead of it," Flagg said Sunday. "We got another game [Monday]. So just trying to get my calories and stay ahead of it and be ready for another one [Monday]."
Flagg said that he prefers smooth peanut butter and grape jelly. He added that he also enjoys sandwiches with peanut butter and banana, while sometimes adding honey.

features.headline: Who has won MLB Rookie of the Year? All-time winners list
features.desc: MLB's Rookie of the Year award is presented to the best rookies of the American and National League. Check out the full list of winners by year.
body: In 1947 and 1948, the Rookie of the Year was given to Major League Baseball's top rookie-eligible player. Since 1949, the award has been presented to a player in the American League and National League.
The Baseball Writers' Association of America votes on the award at the end of each season and before the start of the postseason.

Before 1957, voters used their own judgment to determine which players were considered rookies. After 1957, players were considered rookies if they had fewer than 75 at-bats or 45 innings pitched prior to the season.

This was later changed to 90 at-bats, 45 innings pitched or 45 days of MLB service time. In 1971, the mark was adjusted to 130 at-bats, 50 innings pitched or 45 days of non-September service time. That remains the standard today.
Jackie Robinson was MLB's first Rookie of the Year in 1947. Robinson hit.297 with 12 home runs, 31 doubles, five triples, 48 RBIs and 29 stolen bases for the Brooklyn Dodgers.
The award has been named the Jackie Robinson Award since 1987, the 40th anniversary of Robinson breaking the league's color barrier.

In 2026, Kevin McGonigle of the Detroit Tigers won the award for the American League, while Sal Stewart of the Cincinnati Reds won it for the National League. Here's a look at every rookie who has won the Jackie Robinson Award:
2023: Gunnar Henderson (AL), Corbin Carroll (NL)
2022: Julio Rodriguez (AL), Michael Harris II (NL)
2021: Randy Arozarena (AL), Jonathan India (NL)
2018: Shohei Ohtani (AL), Ronald Acuna Jr. (NL)

features.headline: Who will win MVP? Cy Young? Picks, analysis for 2026 MLB awards week
features.desc: Baseball's best players and managers of 2026 collect their hardware this week — starting Tuesday with the year's top rookies.
body: The baseball offseason has felt pretty normal so far, if you can put the overhanging labor negotiations out of your mind.
Some of that normalcy comes from the gradual easing into the initial phases of the hot stove season — contract options, roster maneuvering, free agency filing — that point toward next season.
That's administrative stuff, though, and not as fun as the parade in Milwaukee — or this week, when MLB hands out its major awards in what closes the books on the 2026 season.

This year's awards week adds a new honor being handed out by the Baseball Writers' Association of America: the Reliever of the Year Award, which recognizes the top bullpen maestro from each league. Here's how this week's schedule lays out:
Tuesday: Manager of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Wednesday: Cy Young and Reliever of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Thursday: MVP (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network)
MLB Network will also air the MLB awards given out during a live ceremony in Las Vegas at 8 p.m. ET on Wednesday.

Honors presented then include the Hank Aaron Award, Comeback Player of the Year, Mariano Rivera & Trevor Hoffman Relievers of the Year, Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter Award and selections for the All-MLB first and second teams.
Finalists for the major awards have already been announced. So let's see how things look before the hardware is handed out. Who might win? Who should win?

Final tally: McGonigle 204 (28 first-place votes), Parker Messick 122 (2), Payton Tolle 54, Munetaka Murakami 39, Carter Jensen 31, Chase DeLauter 23, Kazuma Okamoto 17, Tristan Peters 12, Sam Antonacci 2, Travis Bazzana 2, Walbert Urena 2, Dylan Beavers 1, Henry Bolte 1

features.headline: 'The World Cup never really ended': U.S.-based betting sees rise in wagering on MLS, European soccer
features.desc: Before the World Cup, many wondered if Americans would stick around afterward. Betting data says yes, they did.
body: Soccer was the sport of the summer in the United States this year, as the FIFA World Cup came to 11 American cities (in addition to venues in Canada and Mexico).
Americans embraced the sport fully, supporting tremendous numbers for television viewership and stadium attendance — as well as sports betting handle.
BetMGM said that the World Cup "nearly kept pace with the MLB's rigorous summer schedule" despite there being five times as many baseball games over that time period.

Hard Rock Bet noted the tournament did three times as much handle and brought in double the number of individual bettors as the men's NCAA tournament, which is traditionally the most-bet-on event on the U.S. sports calendar.

In Colorado, which breaks down betting revenue by sport, the World Cup generated $60.2 million, a near 250% increase from the $17.5 million brought in by the previous edition of the tournament in November 2022.
With European league soccer in full swing and Major League Soccer kicking off playoffs, that momentum has continued over for the American sports betting ecosystem.

BetMGM noted that in the two-month period immediately following the conclusion of the 2026 World Cup, the sportsbook saw a 24.5% year-over-year increase in bets and a 34.5% increase in handle on wagers for club soccer.

Hard Rock said there have been nearly 30% more wagers on soccer overall, specifically 43% more in the Premier League and 21% in the Champions League with World Cup stars Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland and Harry Kane attracting double the amount of bets in the competition compared to the same time period last year.
